Cash Flow and Free Cash Flow Margin are used to assess our ability to repay our indebtedness, return capital to our shareholders and fund potential acquisitions without access to external sources of financing for such purposes. We define Free Cash Flow as cash flow from operating activities less investment in capital expenditures. We define Free Cash Flow Margin as Free Cash Flow divided by total revenues. We believe Free Cash Flow and Free Cash Flow Margin are useful because they allow for an effective evaluation of both our operating and financial performance, as well as the capital intensity of our business, and subsequently the ability of our operations to generate cash flow that is available to distribute to our shareholders, reduce leverage or support acquisition activities. Net cash provided by financing activities during the third quarter of 2026 was $74.8 million. Strong Balance Sheet with Ample Liquidity Total liquidity was $126.8 million as of September 30, 2026. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had approximately $110.0 million of available borrowing capacity under its revolving credit facility. Total cash and cash equivalents were $16.8 million as of September 30, 2026, as compared to $39.8 million as of June 30, 2026. The Company had $765.0 million of borrowings outstanding as of September 30, 2026, as compared to $545.2 million outstanding as of June 30, 2026. Subsequent to quarter end, on October 1, 2026, DBR Land Holdings LLC ("OpCo") issued an additional $125.0 million aggregate principal amount of 6.25% fixed-rate senior unsecured notes due 2030 under its existing indenture (the “Additional Notes”). The Additional Notes have terms identical to those of the existing $500 million aggregate principal amount of 6.25% fixed-rate senior 3 unsecured notes due 2030 that were issued in November 2025 (the "Notes"), other than the issue date and issue price. The Additional Notes and the Notes are treated as a single series for all purposes under the existing indenture, bringing the total aggregate principal amount to $625.0 million. Third Quarter 2026 Acquisitions During the third quarter of 2026, the Company acquired approximately 25,000 acres, representing numerous individual strategic transactions across the Company's existing footprint. The acquired acreage includes fee surface and mineral classified surface interests, which enables LandBridge to participate in the upside of minerals production as the surface owner. The acquisitions include material upside tied to further commercialization of the surface estate access and provide access to highly-contiguous surface acreage with attractive, undeveloped pore space, strategically positioned outside of the over-pressured injection zones close to the Stateline region, offering large, active E&P operators a responsible, long-term alternative for produced water disposal. LandBridge is engaged in active discussions with operators, providing strong confidence in its ability to develop and commercialize this pore space, helping to further diversify the asset's cash flows while preserving their long-term, recurring nature.
